_comment: Metals WS2 — DERIVED. No printed answer key; all answers derived for human review.

1.reason: Na (sodium) is the only metal listed; C, N, O are non-metals.

2.reason: Fe is more reactive than Cu, so CuSO4 + Fe gives a displacement reaction. Fe cannot displace Zn, Mg, or Pb (Zn/Mg are more reactive; Pb is more reactive than Fe).

3.reason: Aluminium forms an amphoteric oxide (Al2O3) reacting with both acids and bases; Na/Ca/Cu oxides are basic.

4.reason: Mercury (Hg) is the only metal liquid at room temperature.

5.reason: Royal water = aqua regia = mixture of conc. HCl and conc. HNO3 in 3:1 ratio. X=Aqua regia, Y=HCl, Z=HNO3.

6.reason: The rust-resistant Iron Pillar at Delhi is made of wrought iron.

7.reason: Burning magnesium imparts a dazzling white flame.

8.reason: Zinc amalgam is an alloy of zinc with mercury; Alnico, stainless steel, and solder contain no mercury.

9.reason: Metals show electrical conduction (A), are sonorous (B), and ductile (D); dullness (C) is a non-metal property. So A, B and D.

10.reason: Only aqua regia (HCl:HNO3 = 3:1, tube C) dissolves noble metals Au and Pt; neither conc. HCl nor conc. HNO3 alone (tubes A, B) dissolves them.

11.reason: Sulphurous acid is H2SO3 (H2SO4 is sulphuric acid).

12.reason: Cu is more reactive than Ag, so AgNO3 solution + copper metal gives a displacement reaction. FeSO4+Ag, NaCl+Cu, MgCl2+Al do not (less-reactive metal cannot displace a more-reactive one).

13.reason: Non-metals are electron acceptors; they cannot donate electrons to H+ to liberate H2, so they do not displace hydrogen from acids.

14.reason: Lead is malleable but a poor conductor of electricity; silver and copper are excellent conductors.

15.reason: Platinum (Pt), a noble metal, occurs in the free (native) state in nature.

17.reason: The fountain experiment demonstrates the very high solubility of NH3 (ammonia) gas in water.

18.reason: Activity series (K>Na>Ca>Mg>Al>Zn>Fe>Pb>H>Cu): Mg is below Ca but above Al — true. The other statements contradict the series.

19.reason: W=S (covalent solid, never conducts); X=HCl (conducts only in aqueous solution); Y=Pb (metal, conducts in solid and molten); Z=NaCl (ionic, conducts when molten or in aqueous solution).

20.reason: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of a metal with one or more elements.

21.reason: Cooking utensils need good thermal conductivity (i) and high melting point (iv); electrical conductivity and ductility are irrelevant here.

22.reason: Correct chemistry: Fe in ZnSO4 gives no reaction (Zn more reactive); Zn in FeSO4 reacts, fading colour and depositing Fe. Student C reports Fe/ZnSO4 = no change/no change and Zn/FeSO4 = turned colourless/black deposit, which is correct.

24.reason: In copper pyrites extraction, FeO combines with silica (SiO2) flux to form FeSiO3 (iron silicate) slag.

25.reason: Ductility is the property by which a metal can be drawn into wires.

27.reason: During smelting, flux combines with impurities (gangue) to form a fusible product called slag.

28.reason: A reddish-brown coating of copper deposits on the iron nail; Fe displaces Cu only from copper sulphate solution.

30.reason: Metal + dil. H2SO4 -> metal sulphate + H2; the gas evolved is hydrogen (H2).

32.reason: Fe displaces Cu from CuSO4: blue solution turns green (Fe2+ forms) and a reddish copper coating forms on the nail.

33.reason: In electrolytic refining the IMPURE metal anode dissolves; option C wrongly says the 'pure metal from the anode dissolves', which is the incorrect description.

34.reason: Liquid metal=Mercury(D), best conductor of heat=Silver(A), poorest conductor=Lead(C), cut with a knife=Sodium(B): 1-D, 2-A, 3-C, 4-B.

36.reason: Shiny non-metal=Iodine(c), melts at room temperature=Gallium(b), soft metal=Sodium(d), liquid metal=Mercury(a): (i)-c,(ii)-b,(iii)-d,(iv)-a.

37.reason: Metal-Basic oxides(D), Non-metal-Acidic oxides(A), Amphoteric-Both acidic and basic(C), Salts-Neutral(B): 1-D, 2-A, 3-C, 4-B.

38.reason: Bronze-Copper(d), Stainless steel-Iron(a), Solder-Tin and lead(c), Duralumin-Aluminium(b): (i)-d,(ii)-a,(iii)-c,(iv)-b.

39.reason: Most reactive=Potassium(B), least reactive=Gold(D), metal less reactive than hydrogen=Copper(A), non-metal=Bromine(C): 1-B, 2-D, 3-A, 4-C.

40.reason: Statement A is true (sulphur compounds such as sulpha drugs are medicines) and Statement B is true (cast iron contains about 3-5% carbon); both true.

41.reason: Statement A is false (not all metals form basic oxides; Al/Zn form amphoteric oxides); Statement B is true (a few non-metals such as CO, NO, H2O form neutral oxides).

42.reason: Statement A is true (an alloy has lower electrical conductivity and melting point than its pure metals); Statement B is false (different metals differ in reactivity with water/acids). Option B states this; note option D is printed with identical text.

43.reason: REVIEW: Asks the INCORRECT statement. Mg + steam -> MgO (oxide) + H2, so option B ('steam -> magnesium hydroxide') is the standard textbook error. However option C ('cold water -> magnesium oxide') is also factually wrong (Mg reacts very slowly with cold water to give the hydroxide). The question appears to have two flawed statements; B is the conventionally intended answer.

44.reason: Z=13 protons = Aluminium: (1) forms amphoteric oxide Al2O3, (2) valency 3, (3) chloride AlCl3 = XCl3 — all three statements correct, so (A), (B) and (C).

45.reason: REVIEW: X(2,8)=noble gas/non-metal, Y(2,8,7)=halogen/non-metal, Z(2,8,2)=metal. Asks the INCORRECT statement. Option B (Y non-metal, Z metal) is the only fully correct statement, so A, C and D are all incorrect — the question is defective. A ('Y is a metal') is selected as the clearest single incorrect statement.

46.reason: Soft (cut with a knife), highly reactive in air, reacts vigorously with water — this is sodium (Na).

47.reason: An iron nail in copper sulphate solution turns the blue solution greenish (Fe displaces Cu), so the solution was copper sulphate.

48.reason: Always add acid to water. Piyush adds water to concentrated H2SO4, causing violent exothermic splashing — Piyush is in danger.

23.reason: Metal + dil H2SO4 -> salt + H2. Hydrogen is the gas evolved; it is lighter than air and insoluble in water, which is why the figure collects it over water (downward displacement of water). So the gas is lighter than air and insoluble in water = option D.

26.reason: Rusting needs BOTH air (oxygen) and water. Tube A (nail in water + air) has both -> rusts. Tube B has boiled water (no dissolved air) sealed under oil (no air contact) -> no rust. Tube C has dry air with anhydrous CaCl2 absorbing all moisture (no water) -> no rust. Only Tube A rusts = option C.

29.reason: The figure shows the gas (H2) bubbling up into an upright jar standing in a trough of water, pushing the water down and out. Hydrogen, being light and insoluble, rises up into the jar -> collection by upward displacement of water = option A.

31.reason: The apparatus heats glass-wool soaked in water to produce steam, which passes over a heated metal sample; the hydrogen liberated is collected over water. This is the standard 'action of steam on a metal' experiment = option C.
